body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm adap}\), construct one \(a\)-independent sample-split convex-projection test with rejection probability at most \(\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly over \(\{P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}:d(P)=0\}\), and with power at \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\), where \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)\) is the smallest attainable adaptation factor. The calibration must resample training and testing uncertainty and remain valid on all source and box faces. Invert the resulting family of sublevel-set tests to obtain a lower confidence bound for \(d(P)\) with frontier-order stochastic width.
body.justification: Sharp rates are operational only with a calibration that survives nonregular active faces and unknown proxy strength.
body.gap: Fang and Seo require a fixed cone, while Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos do not analyze a growing image transported by a separately estimated operator.
body.consumer: Wu et al.'s binary-event discrete workflow receives a level-certified rejection rule and a quantitative lower bound on observable misspecification.
